newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Ten million Brazilians lack health care - minister.
newsitem.headline: Ten million Brazilians lack health care - minister.

text.p: More than 10 million Brazilians lack access to basic health care, Health Minister Carlos Alburquerque said on Friday.
The minister announced that the federal government would turn to private health insurers, and state and municipal governments to try to make up the shortfall in health care.
"More than 10 million Brazilians don't even have access to the most basic health care," Alburquerque said.
Brazil's public health service handles 318 million medical cases and 502 million medical exams a year, according to the Health Ministry.
But Alburquerque said this was insufficient and the only way to bridge the gap was to get states and cities more involved in providing health services.
In addition, private health insurers, serving some 38 million Brazilians, frequently failed to pay up, placing health service budgets under great strain, the minister said.
"They are going to pay the government for the services we give their clients," he said.
